newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sept S&P 500s end at record high settlements.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sept S&P 500s end at record high settlements.

text.p: U.S. September Standard & Poor's 500 futures ended at record high settlements, as mutual fund money continued to flood the U.S. stock market, traders and floor analysts said.
They said the ability of the 30-year cash bond yield to back off from the key 6.50 percent level kept fresh the idea that U.S. stocks offer better rates of return than fixed-income instruments.
September S&Ps rose to 968.00, a record high, late in the session after the U.S. T-bond futures market closed for the day with a firm tone.
September S&Ps rallied through a key technical resistance level at 967.75 and now floor analysts are eyeing 970.00 as the next main objective.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's Beige book suggested to some analysts that U.S. interest rates would stay steady in the near-term.
The book, which will be discussed when the Fed's policy committee meets on August 19, said the U.S. economy grew moderately in June and July.
U.S. weekly jobless claims and June wholesale inventories will be released on Thursday morning.
Those reports, coupled with the June consumer credit report at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT, could give both U.S. stock and U.S. bond traders further clues into the state of the U.S. economy.
Nikkei futures also ended sharply higher, with September climbing back to resistance at 19,780 at the close.

Volume for September S&Ps was estimated at 62,000 contracts, with the bulk of trade coming in the latter half of the session. In the first half of the day, locals were forced to cover short positions quickly after dealers made their presence known in the pit as buyers.

Locals pushed and prodded September S&Ps below the pivot point of 956.30 at the opening in search of sell-stop orders. Those orders were found at 955.20, but downside momentum was limited when dealers began buying contracts at the daily low of 953.70, floor sources said.
Arbitrage buy programs were noted at around 5.11 points over the cash index. Fair value for September stood at 4.31 points and arbitrage sell programs were seen at a premium of 3.17 points to cash.

At the end of pit trade, September S&P 500s were up 7.10 at a record high settlement of 963.60, KCBT Value Lines were up 6.70 at 853.20, new composites were 3.80 higher at 498.75, Midcap 400s were 1.75 higher at 321.25, Russell 2000s were up 0.50 at 422.25 and Nikkeis rose 300 at 19,780.
